Serendipitous

sair-uhn-DIP-uh-tuhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Serendipitous is occurring or discovered by happy chance, without being planned.

Their book club's serendipitous choice of venue -- a bookstore that turned out to be hosting the very author they were discussing -- became the story they told for years.

Worked Example

Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin was famously serendipitous -- he simply noticed that mold had accidentally killed the bacteria in a forgotten petri dish.

Nothing about the discovery was planned; a lucky accident led to one of medicine's biggest breakthroughs, which is exactly what serendipitous describes.

How Serendipitous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

fortuitous

fortuitous: a chance happening, especially a lucky one

accidental

accidental: happening by chance, not intended

Antonyms

planned

planned: deliberately arranged in advance

predictable

predictable: able to be foreseen or expected

How Strong Is It? — lucky → providential → serendipitous

lucky vs. serendipitous

lucky vs. serendipitous: having good fortune, without emphasizing a surprising discovery

providential vs. serendipitous

providential vs. serendipitous: seeming almost too perfectly timed to be mere chance

Build the Word

The pieces

root — serendipity

root — serendipity: the occurrence of fortunate discoveries by accident (coined 1754 by Horace Walpole, from the Persian fairy tale 'The Three Princes of Serendip')

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Serendipitous comes straight from the noun serendipity -- 'the occurrence of fortunate discoveries by accident' -- plus -ous, 'full of.' Something serendipitous is simply full of serendipity.

Use the root in a new word: serendipity

Use the root in a new word: serendipity: It was pure serendipity that the two old friends ended up seated next to each other on a flight neither had planned to take.
